1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection. Tripping that device removes every charging session on the branch at once, and in many installations it also removes the auxiliary loads sharing the branch.
4	
5	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
6	
7	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
8	
9	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

1	An apparatus controls charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch whose branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of those vehicle connectors. Each connector channel of the apparatus includes a contactor connected between the electrical branch and a respective vehicle connector, a connector current sensor arranged to measure a connector current delivered through that vehicle connector, and a control-pilot interface, and each connector channel is associated with a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor is arranged to measure a branch current in the electrical branch upstream of the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, so that the aggregate current of the branch is obtained from a measurement that is independent of the per connector measurements.
2	
3	A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor. The controller stores, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. At each allocation interval of a succession of allocation intervals, the controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. The controller sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel and verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel.
4	
5	The branch current sensor serves as an independent safety input. Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device.
6	
7	In further aspects, a contactor is not reclosed until the connector current sensor of its connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels on the branch, and controllers at neighbouring branches, do not restore load simultaneously. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, whereupon the controller inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch and operates a local fault indicator.
8	
9	In further aspects, the controller receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through a network interface while holding a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage the controller continues already authorized charging sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to the branch current sensing described above, and does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.
10	
11	In a further aspect, a service input permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the connector current sensor that responds, the association being stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel, so that a field wiring error cannot cause an assigned current limit to be applied to the wrong vehicle connector.
12

45	The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its management service will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence in the nonvolatile memory 112. Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined. The sequence is uploaded to the management service when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one addressed connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored and the fault indicator 116 is operated. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded, and cause the edge controller 106 to perform the allocation, verification, staged reduction and ordered shedding described above when they are executed by the processing unit 132. The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time. The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106.

The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102.

The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling, and the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

input.summary:
The draft is a well-organised, internally coherent application whose backbone — branch-limited allocation, per-connector verification, staged reduction, ordered contactor shedding, conditional reclosure, welded-contactor isolation, offline authorization, tamper-evident records and commissioning mapping — traces cleanly to input/disclosure.md (which is identical to the single USER message in input/conversation.md). Numerals are used consistently: every numeral in numerals.md labels exactly one part, and each part carries the same numeral everywhere in draft/08-detailed-description.md and in the figure briefs. The Brief Description of the Drawings matches what the four briefs describe, and no numeral is defined twice or reused.

Two mechanical limits on this review: (1) figures/ contains only the four Markdown briefs — there are no rendered-*.png files, and review/figure-audit-evidence.json does not exist in this workspace, so I could not verify pixels, printed numerals, leaders or geometry; the "each described figure has a drawing sheet" and "27 numerals absent from every drawing" mechanical failures are the same fact, and I have not re-reported them as findings. My figure comments are therefore brief-versus-text only. (2) prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references ("| (none) | | |") and the draft contains no [REF:...] citation anywhere, so there is nothing to check under citation honesty; the background makes only uncited general-field statements. findings.title: Hash-chain construction of the tamper-evident meter sequence is not in the disclosure, and is claimed
findings.detail: The disclosure says only that meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded later. It says nothing about how tamper-evidence is achieved. The candidate supplies a specific chained-value construction and then claims it, so the only support for claim 13 is the candidate's own added text.

Candidate claim 13: "each appended meter record carrying a value computed over that meter record together with a preceding state of the tamper-evident local sequence". Candidate ¶41: "Each appended record carries a value computed over that record together with the preceding state of the sequence, so that removal, reordering or alteration of a record is detectable when the sequence is examined."

findings.title: Stored range, per-channel draw and neighbouring-branch coordination added to the randomized recovery delay, and claimed

Claim 5 recites the stored range and the per-channel draw.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶9): "A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero, the control-pilot interface reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired." Candidate claim 5: "to draw the randomized recovery delay within a stored range separately for each connector channel that has been opened." Candidate ¶35: "The randomized recovery delay is drawn by the edge controller 106 within a stored range and is drawn separately for each connector channel, so that ... controllers at neighbouring branches that were disturbed by a common event do not restore their load at the same instant." findings.fix: Cancel claim 5. In ¶35 replace the added sentence with the disclosed condition alone ("A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding.") and delete ", and controllers at neighbouring branches," from summary ¶7.

findings.title: Requested-current cap on the deficit share, and re-offer of the undistributable residue, are not disclosed and are claimed
findings.detail: The disclosure stores a requested current per active connector but says only that the remaining current is distributed according to energy deficit. Candidate claim 9: "wherein the share of the remainder distributed to an active connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that active connector channel, and the controller is configured to offer to the other active connector channels a part of the remainder that is not distributed by reason of that limit." Candidate ¶21: "The share given to a connector channel is limited by the requested current stored for that connector channel, and any part of the remainder that cannot be placed for that reason is offered to the other active connector channels."
findings.fix: Cancel claim 9 and delete the final sentence of ¶21 ("The share given to a connector channel is limited ... offered to the other active connector channels."); the disclosed distribution rule already supported by claim 8 and by the preceding sentences of ¶21 is retained.

findings.title: Fault-indicator response to a commissioning mismatch is not disclosed and is claimed
findings.detail: The disclosure's commissioning process ends at the storage condition: the association is stored only if the sensed channel agrees. It attaches the local fault indicator solely to the welded-contactor condition. The candidate extends the fault indicator to a wiring mismatch and to a no-response case and claims that extension.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶13): "The association is stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector." Disclosure (¶9), the only fault-indicator statement: "The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator." Candidate claim 15: "and to operate a local fault indicator when the responding connector current sensor is the connector current sensor of another connector channel or when no connector current sensor responds." findings.fix: Delete the "and to operate a local fault indicator ..." clause from claim 15, leaving the disclosed storage condition, and in ¶43 replace the sentence with "Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored."

findings.title: Two named ways of obtaining the non-charging branch load, including a dedicated sensor, are added; one is claimed

The candidate supplies a derivation (branch current minus the summed connector currents) and an alternative structural element (a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load 118) that no source mentions, and claim 16 recites the derivation. A derivation that is merely obvious from the disclosed sensors is not source support.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current." Candidate claim 16: "to obtain the measured non-charging branch load as a part of the measured branch current that is not accounted for by a sum of the connector currents measured by the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels."
findings.fix: Cancel claim 16 and delete the two implementation sentences from ¶19, leaving the disclosed statement that the edge controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit.

findings.title: Component-technology and enclosure variants presented as embodiments have no source
findings.detail: None of these variants appears in the disclosure or the conversation. Each is a variant presented as part of the invention and must trace to a source; conventionality and plausibility are not support.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶45: "The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106." Candidate ¶47: "The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. findings.fix: Delete the last sentence of ¶45 and the whole of ¶47. The disclosed parts remain described at ¶¶5, 7 and 9 in the inventor's own terms.

findings.title: DC charging and multi-outlet connector embodiments are added to the invention
findings.detail: The disclosure describes control-pilot current limits sent to vehicles at EV connectors and says nothing about direct current charging, about a control-pilot interface signalling an available current to vehicle-side equipment, or about a connector having more than one physical outlet and being treated as a single channel for allocation and shedding. These are added embodiments and an added allocation/shedding rule.

findings.fix: Delete ¶49 apart from its opening clause, retaining only "The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling."

findings.title: "Galvanic isolation" is a specific characterisation the disclosure does not give the isolated local bus
findings.detail: The sources say only that the controller communicates over "an isolated local bus". The candidate specifies the kind of isolation and recites it as a claim limitation, so claim 10's characterising feature rests on candidate-introduced text rather than on the disclosure. I am flagging this as major rather than critical because "isolated" is the disclosed word and the candidate has narrowed rather than broadened it, but the specific term is still untraced.

Candidate claim 10: "the isolated local bus providing galvanic isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels." Candidate ¶7: "and provides galvanic isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels."
findings.fix: Replace "galvanic isolation" with "isolation" in claim 10 and in ¶7, so both read in the disclosed terms ("the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels").

findings.title: Derivation of the stored requested current is added
findings.detail: The disclosure lists the requested current among the stored per-session values and never says where the value comes from. The candidate asserts two specific sources for it (the channel rating and demand reported over the control pilot). Nothing in the sources says the control-pilot interface reports a demand.

Candidate ¶13: "The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel."
findings.fix: End the sentence after "spare capacity", deleting ", and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel".

findings.title: Token issuer and signature verification against a stored key are added
findings.detail: The disclosure says the controller stores a signed local authorization token that authorizes a connector and has an expiry. It does not say the management service issues it, and it does not disclose a stored verification key inside the controller — that is an added element of the apparatus. The connector-authorizing and expiry attributes are supported; the issuer and the stored key are not.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶11): "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory ... It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired." Candidate ¶37: "The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry.", deleting the issuer and stored-key clauses.

findings.title: Programmed-processor / fixed-logic implementation and the computer-readable-medium claim have no basis in the sources
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 23; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶45 (first two sentences); draft/06-summary.md ¶13
findings.detail: The disclosure describes a controller that performs functions; it never mentions instructions, a program, fixed logic, or a medium. The candidate's own ¶45 is the sole support for claim 23, and under the source-ledger rule the candidate's description cannot support a claim to matter the candidate introduced. I note that input/brief.md asks for "supported statutory classes" — that instruction requires support, and here the support is absent. The method claims (17-22) are unaffected because they recite disclosed controller operations.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶45: "The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded ..." Candidate summary ¶13: "Corresponding methods, and a non-transitory computer-readable medium carrying instructions for performing them, are also disclosed." Disclosure: no occurrence of "instructions", "medium", "processor", "software" or "logic" anywhere in input/disclosure.md or input/conversation.md.
findings.fix: Cancel claim 23, delete the first two sentences of ¶45, and change summary ¶13 to "Corresponding methods are also disclosed."

findings.title: Definition of the energy-deficit value states a baseline the sources do not give
findings.detail: The disclosure names an "energy-deficit value" without defining it. The candidate fixes it as the shortfall measured against the energy the session would have received at its requested current, and states that it is updated as energy is metered at the channel. This is a reasonable reading of the term, but the specific baseline and the update mechanism are candidate-supplied; claim 8's "larger deficit, larger share" rule does not depend on them.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value." Candidate ¶13: "The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel."
findings.fix: Shorten to "The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session."

findings.title: Definition bounding the leakage threshold is added
findings.detail: The disclosure uses "leakage threshold" as a bare term. The candidate defines it by two bounds (below the smallest session current, above the residual measurement of an open channel), which is an added quantitative relationship rather than a restatement. Claim 6 and claim 20 recite only the disclosed threshold, so removing the definition costs no claim support.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶9): "A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command." Candidate ¶33: "The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded."
findings.fix: Reduce to "The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded."

findings.title: Safety reserve and shedding order are placed in nonvolatile memory 112, which the sources reserve for the token and the last accepted branch limit
findings.detail: The disclosure calls the reserve "configurable" and the shedding order "stored" but assigns neither to a particular memory; the only contents it gives the nonvolatile memory are the signed token and the last accepted branch limit. Locating these two values in element 112 is an added structural relationship. It contradicts nothing, hence minor.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶11): "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory." Candidate ¶19: "The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin, held in the nonvolatile memory 112 ..." Candidate ¶29: "The shedding order is held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed."
findings.fix: Delete ", held in the nonvolatile memory 112" from ¶19 and change ¶29 to "The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed."

findings.title: Examples of the non-charging load are supplied by the candidate
findings.detail: The disclosure refers only to a "measured non-charging branch load" as a quantity subtracted from the branch limit. The presence of non-charging load on the branch follows from that, but the named examples are candidate-supplied and appear in the description of the numbered part 118 and hence of FIG. 1.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶3: "A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command, such as lighting, ventilation or refrigeration equipment." Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit".
findings.fix: Delete ", such as lighting, ventilation or refrigeration equipment" from ¶3; the generic description of element 118 is retained.

findings.title: Attribution of the shedding order to the site operator's choice is untraced
findings.detail: The disclosure says the shedding order is stored; it does not say who determines it. Attributing the order to the site operator adds a configuration relationship not present in the sources.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶29: "Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in an order the site operator has chosen, with the remaining connector channels still charging." Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶9): "the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit."
findings.fix: Replace "in an order the site operator has chosen" with "in the stored shedding order".

findings.title: Claim 2 attaches the connector-level trigger to the branch-level reduced pilot command
findings.detail: The description defines two distinct reduced pilot commands: one issued at the connector verification step 208 because a channel's measured connector current exceeds its assigned limit, and one issued at the staged reduction step 210 because the measured branch current exceeds the branch limit. Claim 1 recites only the second ("responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit"). Claim 2 then makes "the reduced pilot command" — i.e. the branch-triggered one — the command addressed to the channel identified from the connector current sensors, a combination the description does not state at either step. I am marking this minor because both underlying behaviours are described; it is the antecedent linkage that is loose.
findings.evidence: Claim 1: "send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit". Claim 2: "to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel". Candidate ¶25: "A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel". Candidate ¶27: "When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval."
findings.fix: Add to ¶27, after "sends a reduced pilot command", the clause "which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit," so that the description states the combination claim 2 recites.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief shows welded-contactor isolation flowing unconditionally into conditional reclosure
findings.where: figures/fig-04.md, "Structures and relationships" items 7-8 and the connecting-arrow sentence; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶33
findings.detail: The brief places the welded-contactor isolation step 214 and the conditional reclosure step 216 in a single column joined by plain directed arrows, so the depicted flow makes reclosure the unconditional successor of welded-contactor isolation. The description states the opposite for that condition: on a welded contactor the other contactors are inhibited and the condition cannot be cleared from the controller. Because no rendered image exists in figures/, I verified this against the brief only, and mark it minor for that reason.
findings.evidence: figures/fig-04.md: "7. rectangle, the welded-contactor isolation step; 8. rectangle, the conditional reclosure step, at the bottom." and "A straight vertical solid line with an arrowhead at its lower end joins each shape to the shape below it, the arrowhead touching the upper edge of the lower shape." Candidate ¶33: "the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load ... the welded contactor being a condition that cannot be cleared from the edge controller 106 and that requires attention at the equipment."
findings.fix: In figures/fig-04.md, state that the line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step is taken only when no welded-contactor condition has been recorded, by adding after the connecting-arrow sentence: "The line from the seventh shape to the eighth shape carries no further branching; where a welded-contactor condition has been recorded the flow ends at the seventh shape, and this is shown by a short line leaving the right edge of the seventh shape and ending in an arrowhead at a small solid terminator to its right."

findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit to obtain an available charging current." Candidate ¶19: "In one implementation it is obtained from the branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors as that part of the measured branch current which is not accounted for by the sum of the measured connector currents. In another implementation a dedicated sensor at the non-charging load 118 reports it." Candidate claim 16: "to obtain the measured non-charging branch load as a part of the measured branch current that is not accounted for by a sum of the connector currents measured by the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels."
findings.fix: Cancel claim 16 and delete the two implementation sentences from ¶19, leaving the disclosed statement that the edge controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit.

findings.title: Component-technology and enclosure variants presented as embodiments have no source
findings.detail: None of these variants appears in the disclosure or the conversation. The disclosure names only "a controllable contactor", "a connector current sensor", "a branch current sensor" and "an isolated local bus", and says nothing about sensor technology, solid-state switching, bus media, or how the channels and controller are housed. Each is a variant presented as part of the invention and must trace to a source; conventionality and plausibility are not support.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶45: "The branch current sensor 104 and the connector current sensors may be current transformers, Hall effect sensors, shunt based sensors or any other sensors that report a current to the edge controller 106." Candidate ¶47: "The isolated local bus 108 may be a serial bus with galvanic isolation at each connector channel, an optically isolated link, or another isolated interconnection. The contactors may be electromechanical contactors or solid state switching devices having a controllable open state, and the connector channels may be housed in one enclosure with the edge controller 106 or distributed among separate enclosures along the branch conductor 102." Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶5), the whole of what the sources say on these parts: "Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier. A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors. A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus."
findings.fix: Delete the last sentence of ¶45 and the whole of ¶47. The disclosed parts remain described at ¶¶5, 7 and 9 in the inventor's own terms.

findings.title: DC charging and multi-outlet connector embodiments are added to the invention
findings.detail: The disclosure describes control-pilot current limits sent to vehicles at EV connectors and says nothing about direct current charging, about a control-pilot interface signalling an available current to vehicle-side equipment, or about a connector having more than one physical outlet and being treated as a single channel for allocation and shedding. findings.evidence: Candidate ¶49: "the installation 100 may serve alternating current charging, direct current charging in which the control-pilot interface signals the available current to the vehicle side equipment, or a mixture of the two on one branch. Where a connector channel serves a connector with more than one physical outlet, the connector channel is treated as one connector channel for the purposes of the allocation and of the shedding order." Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor."
findings.fix: Delete ¶49 apart from its opening clause, retaining only "The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling."

findings.title: "Galvanic isolation" is a specific characterisation the disclosure does not give the isolated local bus
findings.detail: The sources say only that the controller communicates over "an isolated local bus". The candidate specifies the kind of isolation and recites it as a claim limitation, so claim 10's characterising feature rests on candidate-introduced text rather than on the disclosure. I am flagging this as major rather than critical because "isolated" is the disclosed word and the candidate has narrowed rather than broadened it, but the specific term is still untraced.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶5): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." Candidate claim 10: "the isolated local bus providing galvanic isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels." Candidate ¶7: "and provides galvanic isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels."
findings.fix: Replace "galvanic isolation" with "isolation" in claim 10 and in ¶7, so both read in the disclosed terms ("the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels").

findings.title: Derivation of the stored requested current is added
findings.detail: The disclosure lists the requested current among the stored per-session values and never says where the value comes from. The candidate asserts two specific sources for it (the channel rating and demand reported over the control pilot). Nothing in the sources says the control-pilot interface reports a demand.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "The controller stores, for each active connector, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value." Candidate ¶13: "The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity, and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel."
findings.fix: End the sentence after "spare capacity", deleting ", and is obtained from the rating of the connector channel and from the demand reported through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel".

findings.title: Token issuer and signature verification against a stored key are added
findings.detail: The disclosure says the controller stores a signed local authorization token that authorizes a connector and has an expiry. It does not say the management service issues it, and it does not disclose a stored verification key inside the controller — that is an added element of the apparatus. The connector-authorizing and expiry attributes are supported; the issuer and the stored key are not.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶11): "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory ... It does not start a newly connected session unless the local token authorizes that connector and has not expired." Candidate ¶37: "The signed local authorization token is issued by the management service, carries a signature that the edge controller 106 verifies against a stored key, names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry.", deleting the issuer and stored-key clauses.

findings.title: Programmed-processor / fixed-logic implementation and the computer-readable-medium claim have no basis in the sources
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 23; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶45 (first two sentences); draft/06-summary.md ¶13
findings.detail: The disclosure describes a controller that performs functions; it never mentions instructions, a program, fixed logic, or a medium. The candidate's own ¶45 is the sole support for claim 23, and under the source-ledger rule the candidate's description cannot support a claim to matter the candidate introduced. I note that input/brief.md asks for "supported statutory classes" — that instruction requires support, and here the support is absent. The method claims (17-22) are unaffected because they recite disclosed controller operations.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶45: "The processing unit 132, the session record store 134 and the functions attributed to the edge controller 106 may be implemented by a programmed processor executing instructions held in the nonvolatile memory 112, by fixed logic, or by a combination of the two. The instructions may be carried on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, such as the nonvolatile memory 112 or a medium from which the nonvolatile memory 112 is loaded ..." Candidate summary ¶13: "Corresponding methods, and a non-transitory computer-readable medium carrying instructions for performing them, are also disclosed." Disclosure: no occurrence of "instructions", "medium", "processor", "software" or "logic" anywhere in input/disclosure.md or input/conversation.md.
findings.fix: Cancel claim 23, delete the first two sentences of ¶45, and change summary ¶13 to "Corresponding methods are also disclosed."

findings.title: Definition of the energy-deficit value states a baseline the sources do not give
findings.detail: The disclosure names an "energy-deficit value" without defining it. The candidate fixes it as the shortfall measured against the energy the session would have received at its requested current, and states that it is updated as energy is metered at the channel. This is a reasonable reading of the term, but the specific baseline and the update mechanism are candidate-supplied; claim 8's "larger deficit, larger share" rule does not depend on them.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "a minimum sustaining current, and an energy-deficit value." Candidate ¶13: "The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session relative to the energy the session would have received had its requested current been served, and is updated by the processing unit 132 as energy is metered at the connector channel."
findings.fix: Shorten to "The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session."

findings.title: Definition bounding the leakage threshold is added
findings.detail: The disclosure uses "leakage threshold" as a bare term. The candidate defines it by two bounds (below the smallest session current, above the residual measurement of an open channel), which is an added quantitative relationship rather than a restatement. Claim 6 and claim 20 recite only the disclosed threshold, so removing the definition costs no claim support.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶9): "A welded-contactor condition is recorded when connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command." Candidate ¶33: "The leakage threshold is a stored current below the smallest current a charging session draws and above the residual measurement of a connector channel that is open, so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded."
findings.fix: Reduce to "The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded."

findings.title: Safety reserve and shedding order are placed in nonvolatile memory 112, which the sources reserve for the token and the last accepted branch limit
findings.detail: The disclosure calls the reserve "configurable" and the shedding order "stored" but assigns neither to a particular memory; the only contents it gives the nonvolatile memory are the signed token and the last accepted branch limit. Locating these two values in element 112 is an added structural relationship. It contradicts nothing, hence minor.
findings.evidence: Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶11): "it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory." Candidate ¶19: "The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin, held in the nonvolatile memory 112 ..." Candidate ¶29: "The shedding order is held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed."
findings.fix: Delete ", held in the nonvolatile memory 112" from ¶19 and change ¶29 to "The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed."

findings.title: Examples of the non-charging load are supplied by the candidate
findings.detail: The disclosure refers only to a "measured non-charging branch load" as a quantity subtracted from the branch limit. The presence of non-charging load on the branch follows from that, but the named examples are candidate-supplied and appear in the description of the numbered part 118 and hence of FIG. 1.

Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶7): "the controller subtracts measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch limit".

findings.title: Attribution of the shedding order to the site operator's choice is untraced
findings.detail: The disclosure says the shedding order is stored; it does not say who determines it. Attributing the order to the site operator adds a configuration relationship not present in the sources.
findings.evidence: Candidate ¶29: "Ordered shedding under measurement replaces that outcome with the loss of as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in an order the site operator has chosen, with the remaining connector channels still charging." Disclosure (input/disclosure.md ¶9): "the controller opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit."
findings.fix: Replace "in an order the site operator has chosen" with "in the stored shedding order".

findings.title: Claim 2 attaches the connector-level trigger to the branch-level reduced pilot command
findings.detail: The description defines two distinct reduced pilot commands: one issued at the connector verification step 208 because a channel's measured connector current exceeds its assigned limit, and one issued at the staged reduction step 210 because the measured branch current exceeds the branch limit. Claim 1 recites only the second ("responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit"). Claim 2 then makes "the reduced pilot command" — i.e. the branch-triggered one — the command addressed to the channel identified from the connector current sensors, a combination the description does not state at either step. I am marking this minor because both underlying behaviours are described; it is the antecedent linkage that is loose.
findings.evidence: Claim 1: "send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit". Claim 2: "to identify, from the connector current sensors, an active connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds the assigned current limit of that active connector channel, and to send the reduced pilot command to the identified active connector channel". Candidate ¶25: "A connector channel whose measured connector current exceeds its assigned current limit has not complied, and the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command to that connector channel". Candidate ¶27: "When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command and starts a verification interval."
findings.fix: Add to ¶27, after "sends a reduced pilot command", the clause "which it directs to a connector channel identified at the connector verification step 208 as drawing more than its assigned current limit," so that the description states the combination claim 2 recites.
